# Flows

_nextop 0.1.3_

One flow per file: `flows/<name>.json`. `nextop run` uses `main` (or the only flow) unless `--flow` is given.

```json
{
  "blocks": [
    { "id": "start", "type": "function", "function": "take_request" },
    { "id": "sum",  "type": "worker", "worker": "summarizer" },
    { "id": "crit", "type": "worker", "worker": "critic" },
    { "id": "edit", "type": "worker", "worker": "editor" }
  ],
  "lines": [
    { "from": "start.request", "to": "sum" },
    { "from": "start.request", "to": "crit" },
    { "from": "sum.summary",   "to": "edit" },
    { "from": "crit.concerns", "to": "edit" }
  ]
}
```

- `from` is always `<block_id>.<terminal>`. There is no built-in input block: the flow input (`--input`)
  goes to start functions, functions with `START = True` (see functions/README.md), and to start workers,
  worker blocks with no incoming line (see workers/README.md).
- Worker, function and split blocks take any number of lines and start once every line has delivered;
  each line becomes one section of the input (`<block>/<terminal>`). A gather block takes exactly one.
  There is no merge block: to combine inputs in a special way, write a function that does it.
- `"review": true` on a worker block stops the run after it until a person decides:
  `nextop review <run_id> <block> approve` or `... redo --note "what to change"` (the note goes into the
  block's input). `nextop run --step` makes every worker block a review point. Not inside parallel sections.
- `to` is a block id, or `<worker block>.question` for an open question (its output is then `answer`;
  see workers/README.md).
- No cycles, except back lines from switch blocks (below). An output nobody receives is a final result.
- Share lines of file servers (file_servers/README.md) also set order: a receiver starts after its senders.
- The same worker may sit in several blocks.
- `layout` (block positions) is written by `nextop studio`; runs ignore it. Keep it when editing by hand.

## Parallel sections (split and gather)

Do the same work for many pieces at once: a `split` block starts a section, a `gather` block ends it,
and every block between them is copied once per piece (`review@1`, `review@2`, ...) and run in parallel.

```json
{ "id": "split",  "type": "split", "function": "split_items", "parallel": 3, "max_copies": 50 },
{ "id": "gather", "type": "gather" },
{ "from": "research.notes", "to": "split" }, { "from": "split.piece", "to": "review" },
{ "from": "review.picks", "to": "write" },   { "from": "write.report", "to": "gather" },
{ "from": "gather.gathered", "to": "editor" }
```

- How to split is your code: a split function (`KIND = "split"` in functions/) returns a list of pieces.
- `parallel`: copies running at once; `max_copies` (default 50): more pieces stop the run.
- Each copy gets one piece through `split.piece`; `gather.gathered` is the list of results in piece order.
- A split function may declare `OUTPUTS` (several terminals): each piece is then `{terminal: value}` and a
  block gets only the terminals its lines come from (`split.<terminal>`). `"from": "<input terminal>"` on a
  terminal says which input it was cut from; the receiver's input heading then names the block that wrote it.
- Every path from a split must reach the same gather; no lines leave or enter the section otherwise;
  no nested sections. Files shared inside a section stay in the same copy (`photo@2` -> `planner@2`).
- A failed copy lets the others finish; the run stops at the gather and `nextop resume` runs only failed copies.
- Each copy has its own records folder (`blocks/review@2/`).

## Switch blocks (branches and loops)

A switch block sends the run one way out of several. Its switch function lists its cases in `CASES`; they are the
block's output terminals. `run()` returns one case and a value: every line of that case gets the value, the lines
of every other case are closed. Each case may have any number of lines. A line back to an earlier block is a loop.

```json
{ "id": "check", "type": "switch", "function": "check_score", "max_iterations": 3 },
{ "from": "review.review", "to": "check" }, { "from": "write.draft", "to": "check" },
{ "from": "check.pass", "to": "edit" },
{ "from": "check.fail", "to": "write" }
```

- The choice is your code: a switch function (`KIND = "switch"`, `CASES = ["pass", "fail"]`, see
  functions/README.md) returns exactly one `{case: value}`.
- Cases not taken are closed: a block whose lines are all closed is skipped (`_skipped`); a block with several
  lines runs once each line has arrived or closed, without the closed ones (so two ways can meet again).
  A worker's optional output terminal that it did not send closes its lines the same way; functions and switch
  functions get no key for a closed line (use `inputs.get(...)`).
- Back line: a line from a switch block to a block before it. Taking it runs that block and every block after it
  again (each adds 1 to its own iteration); blocks before it keep their results. The value goes to the target's
  input as switch feedback (workers: a section "Switch feedback from ... - iteration n"; functions: the key
  `<switch>/<case>`). Iteration 1 has no feedback: say in the mission what to do when there is one.
- A case may have several back lines; only the blocks they point to get the switch feedback.
- Any number of switch blocks work under that one rule: in a row, nested (a loop inside a loop) or partly
  overlapping. An outer switch that sends a whole inner loop again restarts the inner switch's iteration count
  (a switch going back into the middle of a loop does not, so every loop ends at its max_iterations).
- Records: `switch_log.jsonl` gets one line per choice before the run acts on it (the switch log; resume trusts
  only it for switches). Blocks a back line can send again keep `blocks/<id>/iter-<n>/attempt-<m>/`, n counted
  per block; `iterations.json` of a switch block is a view of its lines. Resume keeps a block whose current
  iteration finished and runs everything else again (and every block after it).
- `max_iterations` (function `MAX_ITERATIONS`, else the block, else project defaults, default 3): going past it fails
  the switch block. A loop holds a parallel section whole (a back line to the split block or before it), or sits
  wholly inside one: a switch block inside a section loops per copy (only copy 3 runs again when copy 3 fails;
  `blocks/b2@3/iter-2/`, `check@3/iterations.json`).
- Inside a copy, function input keys name blocks without the copy number (`b2/result`, not `b2@3/result`).
